Executive Director Corner
Happy July, everyone!

It’s been an amazing summer so far of cookouts, nights spent with friends, and of course, refreshing Happy Hours to help us cool down. In our childhoods, it was around this time of year that many of us started looking towards the dreaded return to the classroom – but here at our campus, the middle of July means that the party is just getting started.

As we head deeper into the season, there’s still plenty to look forward to around campus. From live entertainment and themed events to afternoons spent outside enjoying the sunshine, summer always has a way of bringing people together. It’s been wonderful seeing everyone catching up with neighbors, welcoming visiting family members, and making the most of these longer days. We hope you’ll continue joining us for all the fun, laughter, and little moments that make this time of year so special.

Have a great month!

Yours in Service,

Sean Medsker

Executive Director

Legacy News
As the days grow warmer and brighter, our residents have been enjoying a variety of activities like gardening and outdoor games! We love spending time together during our monthly family get togethers- can’t wait for the cookout this month!

This month join us in celebrating the Sampson’s 63rd Wedding Anniversary!

Families are always encouraged to share photos, stories, and memories that can be incorporated into reminiscing activities.

Farmer’s Market…Farmers’ Market…
Farmer’s Market…Farmers’ Market….Farmers Market…? However it’s spelled, we had such a great time at ours! We hope the smiles on all your faces were as genuine and filled with joy as they appeared! What was your favorite vendor/booth?

“Then & Now
“Then & Now - A 250-Year Journey Through Transportation”

As America celebrates its 250th anniversary in 2026, transportation offers a fascinating look at how far our nation has
As America celebrates its 250th anniversary in 2026, transportation offers a fascinating look at how far our nation has come. From horse-drawn wagons to electric vehicles, the way Americans travel reflects two and a half centuries of innovation and progress.

In 1776, most people traveled on foot, horseback, or by wagon
In 1776, most people traveled on foot, horseback, or by wagon. Roads were often rough dirt paths, and long-distance journeys could take days or even weeks. Traveling from one colony to another required patience, endurance, and careful planning. For many Americans, exploring far beyond their hometown was rare.

During the 1800s, canals, steamboats, and railroads transformed transportation
During the 1800s, canals, steamboats, and railroads transformed transportation. The expansion of railroads connected distant communities and helped businesses grow. People and goods could move across the country faster than ever before, helping to unite a young nation.

The twentieth century introduced the automobile and commercial air travel
The twentieth century introduced the automobile and commercial air travel. Cars gave families greater freedom to travel, while highways connected cities across the country. Airplanes made cross-country trips possible in just hours instead of days.

Today, Americans enjoy transportation technologies that would have seemed unimaginable in 1776
Today, Americans enjoy transportation technologies that would have seemed unimaginable in 1776. GPS navigation, electric vehicles, ride-sharing services, and advanced aircraft make travel faster, safer, and more convenient than ever.

As we commemorate 250 years of American history, transportation reminds us of our nation's spirit of invention and deter
As we commemorate 250 years of American history, transportation reminds us of our nation's spirit of invention and determination. While the methods have changed dramatically, the desire to explore, connect, and move forward remains as strong today as it was at America's founding.

Do you have a talent you’d like to have featured in our monthly newsletter? This could be an article, creative writing, a comic, poem, photo, anything! Talk to Sierra Fletcher (Life Enrichment Director) to find out how to be included.
